_about: Hand-checked pregnancy information for common medicines and supplements. Tiers per trimester: generally_used | caution | avoid. 'from_month' raises the tier from that month of pregnancy on. These are screening labels for patients, not prescribing advice; every screen tells the patient to confirm with her doctor. Review with a clinician before release.

ingredients.name: Folic acid
ingredients.note: Recommended before and during pregnancy to prevent neural tube defects.

ingredients.name: Iron (ferrous sulfate, fumarate, ascorbate, carbonyl iron)
ingredients.note: Recommended in pregnancy to prevent and treat anaemia.

timing.food: Take between meals, ideally with orange juice or other vitamin C. Not with tea, coffee or milk.

ingredients.name: Calcium (carbonate, citrate)
ingredients.note: Often recommended from the second trimester, especially where diets are low in calcium.

ingredients.name: Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol)
ingredients.note: Usual supplement doses are commonly used. Very high doses only if your doctor prescribed them.

ingredients.name: Vitamin B12
ingredients.note: Commonly used, especially in vegetarian diets.

ingredients.name: Vitamin B complex
ingredients.note: Usual supplement doses are commonly used.

ingredients.name: Vitamin C
ingredients.note: Usual doses are commonly used and help iron absorption.

ingredients.name: Prenatal multivitamin
ingredients.note: Pregnancy-specific multivitamins are commonly used. Avoid general multivitamins that contain vitamin A (retinol).

ingredients.name: Vitamin A (retinol), high dose
ingredients.note: High-dose vitamin A (retinol) can harm the baby. Avoid supplements and cod liver oil that contain retinol unless your doctor prescribed them.

ingredients.name: Omega-3 / DHA
ingredients.note: Commonly used. Choose purified fish oil or algal DHA, not cod liver oil.

ingredients.name: Magnesium supplement
ingredients.note: Usual supplement doses are commonly used.

ingredients.name: Zinc
ingredients.note: Usual supplement doses are commonly used.

ingredients.name: Paracetamol (acetaminophen)
ingredients.note: The usual first choice for pain or fever in pregnancy. Use the lowest dose that works for the shortest time, and no more than 4 g a day in total (watch for paracetamol in cold and flu medicines).

ingredients.name: Ibuprofen
ingredients.note: Avoid from about 20 weeks: it can reduce the baby's amniotic fluid and affect the baby's heart. Earlier in pregnancy only if your doctor advises.
ingredients.source: FDA Drug Safety Communication on NSAIDs (2020); NHS

ingredients.name: Diclofenac
ingredients.note: Avoid from about 20 weeks (NSAID). Earlier in pregnancy only if your doctor advises.
ingredients.source: FDA Drug Safety Communication on NSAIDs (2020)

ingredients.name: Naproxen
ingredients.note: Avoid from about 20 weeks (NSAID). Earlier in pregnancy only if your doctor advises.
ingredients.source: FDA Drug Safety Communication on NSAIDs (2020)

ingredients.name: Mefenamic acid
ingredients.note: Avoid from about 20 weeks (NSAID). Often sold for period pain; usually not needed in pregnancy.
ingredients.source: FDA Drug Safety Communication on NSAIDs (2020)

ingredients.name: Aspirin

low_dose.note: Low-dose aspirin (75-150 mg) is commonly prescribed in pregnancy to lower the risk of pre-eclampsia. Take it only as your doctor prescribed and don't stop without asking.

ingredients.note: Pain-relief doses of aspirin are avoided from about 20 weeks. Low-dose aspirin (75-150 mg) prescribed by a doctor is different and commonly used.
ingredients.source: ACOG Committee Opinion 743; FDA Drug Safety Communication on NSAIDs (2020)

ingredients.name: Tramadol
ingredients.note: Only if your doctor prescribed it. Regular use late in pregnancy can cause withdrawal symptoms in the newborn.

ingredients.name: Codeine
ingredients.note: Only if your doctor prescribed it, for the shortest time. Found in some cough syrups.

ingredients.name: Dicyclomine (dicycloverine)
ingredients.note: Limited information in pregnancy. Use only if your doctor advises.

ingredients.name: Doxylamine
ingredients.note: With vitamin B6, a common first treatment for pregnancy nausea. It causes drowsiness.

ingredients.name: Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine)
ingredients.note: Commonly used for pregnancy nausea.

ingredients.name: Ondansetron
ingredients.note: Used for severe nausea and vomiting. Some studies suggest a small increase in certain birth defects with first-trimester use, so it's usually a second choice early on.

ingredients.name: Metoclopramide
ingredients.note: Commonly used short term for nausea and vomiting.

ingredients.name: Domperidone
ingredients.note: Limited information in pregnancy. Use only if your doctor advises.

ingredients.name: Antacid (aluminium / magnesium hydroxide)
ingredients.note: Commonly used for heartburn.

timing.food: Best taken after meals or at bedtime.

ingredients.name: Ranitidine
ingredients.note: Withdrawn in many countries (2020) because of an impurity (NDMA). Ask your doctor about an alternative such as famotidine.

ingredients.name: Famotidine
ingredients.note: Commonly used for heartburn when antacids aren't enough.

ingredients.name: Omeprazole
ingredients.note: Commonly used for heartburn when other treatments aren't enough.

ingredients.name: Pantoprazole
ingredients.note: Used for heartburn when other treatments aren't enough. Less information than omeprazole.

ingredients.name: Lactulose
ingredients.note: Commonly used for constipation (as is fibre like isabgol).

ingredients.name: Loperamide
ingredients.note: Short-term use only if your doctor advises. Drink plenty of fluids.

ingredients.name: Levothyroxine (thyroxine)
ingredients.note: Important to keep taking in pregnancy; the dose often needs to go up. Your doctor will check your thyroid levels.

timing.food: Take on an empty stomach, 30-60 minutes before breakfast.

ingredients.name: Metformin
ingredients.note: Used for gestational diabetes and PCOS under your doctor's care.

ingredients.name: Insulin
ingredients.note: The standard treatment for diabetes in pregnancy.

ingredients.name: Glibenclamide (glyburide)
ingredients.note: Sometimes used for gestational diabetes; insulin or metformin are usually preferred.

ingredients.name: Glimepiride
ingredients.note: Usually switched to insulin or metformin in pregnancy. Don't stop on your own; ask your doctor.

ingredients.name: Labetalol
ingredients.note: A first-choice medicine for high blood pressure in pregnancy.

ingredients.name: Nifedipine
ingredients.note: Commonly used for high blood pressure in pregnancy.

ingredients.name: Methyldopa
ingredients.note: Long used for high blood pressure in pregnancy.

ingredients.name: Atenolol
ingredients.note: Beta-blockers other than labetalol may affect the baby's growth. Your doctor may switch you; don't stop on your own.

ingredients.name: ACE inhibitor (enalapril, ramipril, lisinopril, ...)
ingredients.note: Can harm the baby's kidneys and growth, especially after the first trimester. Contact your doctor promptly to switch; don't just stop a blood pressure medicine without advice.

ingredients.name: Angiotensin receptor blocker (losartan, telmisartan, ...)
ingredients.note: Can harm the baby's kidneys and growth, especially after the first trimester. Contact your doctor promptly to switch.

ingredients.name: Statin (atorvastatin, rosuvastatin, ...)
ingredients.note: Usually stopped during pregnancy. Ask your doctor.

ingredients.name: Enoxaparin / heparin
ingredients.note: The usual blood thinner in pregnancy, prescribed by your doctor.

ingredients.name: Warfarin
ingredients.note: Can cause birth defects. Usually switched to heparin. Contact your doctor promptly; don't stop without advice.

ingredients.name: Progesterone / dydrogesterone
ingredients.note: Prescribed in some pregnancies (for example after bleeding or for a short cervix). Take as your doctor prescribed.

ingredients.name: Amoxicillin (with or without clavulanate)
ingredients.note: Penicillins are commonly used in pregnancy. Finish the course.

ingredients.name: Cephalosporin (cefixime, cefuroxime, cephalexin, ...)
ingredients.note: Commonly used in pregnancy. Finish the course.

ingredients.name: Azithromycin
ingredients.note: Commonly used in pregnancy.

ingredients.name: Clindamycin
ingredients.note: Commonly used in pregnancy.

ingredients.name: Metronidazole
ingredients.note: Used in pregnancy for some infections (tinidazole is usually avoided).

ingredients.name: Nitrofurantoin
ingredients.note: Used for urine infections. Usually avoided near the due date (from about 38 weeks) and often second choice in the first trimester.

ingredients.name: Co-trimoxazole (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole)
ingredients.note: Trimethoprim works against folate, so it's usually avoided in the first trimester; sulfonamides are usually avoided near the due date. Only if your doctor advises.

ingredients.name: Tetracycline antibiotic (doxycycline, minocycline, ...)
ingredients.note: Can stain the baby's teeth and affect bone growth after about 15 weeks. Usually avoided in pregnancy.

ingredients.name: Fluoroquinolone antibiotic (ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, ...)
ingredients.note: Usually avoided in pregnancy when other antibiotics will work. Ask your doctor about an alternative.

ingredients.name: Aminoglycoside (gentamicin, streptomycin, ...)
ingredients.note: Can affect the baby's hearing. Used only for serious infections in hospital.

ingredients.name: Fluconazole (oral)
ingredients.note: Oral antifungals are usually avoided, especially in the first trimester; creams or pessaries (clotrimazole) are preferred for thrush.

ingredients.name: Clotrimazole (cream or pessary)
ingredients.note: Creams and pessaries are commonly used for thrush in pregnancy.

ingredients.name: Hydroxychloroquine
ingredients.note: Usually continued in pregnancy for lupus and similar conditions.

ingredients.name: Cetirizine / loratadine
ingredients.note: Non-drowsy antihistamines commonly used for allergies.

ingredients.name: Chlorphenamine / pheniramine
ingredients.note: Drowsy antihistamines. Commonly used, but avoid regular use close to the due date.

ingredients.name: Montelukast
ingredients.note: Can be continued for asthma if it helps you.

ingredients.name: Salbutamol (albuterol) inhaler
ingredients.note: Keep using your asthma inhalers; uncontrolled asthma is riskier for the baby.

ingredients.name: Budesonide / steroid inhaler
ingredients.note: Keep using your preventer inhaler.

ingredients.name: Prednisolone (oral steroid)
ingredients.note: Used when needed for conditions like asthma or lupus, and as injections to help the baby's lungs before an early birth. Take only as prescribed.

ingredients.name: Sertraline / citalopram / escitalopram
ingredients.note: Often continued when the benefit outweighs the risk. Don't stop suddenly; discuss with your doctor.

ingredients.name: Paroxetine
ingredients.note: Linked to heart defects with first-trimester use; other antidepressants are usually preferred. Don't stop suddenly; discuss with your doctor.

ingredients.name: Valproate (sodium valproate, divalproex)
ingredients.note: High risk of birth defects and developmental problems. Contact your doctor urgently, but don't stop it suddenly: a seizure can also harm you and the baby.

ingredients.name: Carbamazepine / phenytoin
ingredients.note: Some risk of birth defects; extra folic acid is usually prescribed. Don't stop suddenly; your doctor will review the medicine and dose.

ingredients.name: Lamotrigine / levetiracetam
ingredients.note: Among the preferred epilepsy medicines in pregnancy; levels change, so your doctor will monitor. Don't stop on your own.

ingredients.name: Lithium
ingredients.note: Needs close monitoring in pregnancy. Don't stop on your own.

ingredients.name: Isotretinoin / acitretin
ingredients.note: Causes serious birth defects. Stop and contact your doctor straight away if you are pregnant.

ingredients.name: Retinoid creams (tretinoin, adapalene)
ingredients.note: Usually avoided in pregnancy. Ask about other acne treatments.

ingredients.name: Methotrexate
ingredients.note: Causes miscarriage and birth defects. Contact your doctor straight away.

ingredients.name: Misoprostol / mifepristone
ingredients.note: Causes contractions and pregnancy loss. Only under specific medical care.

ingredients.name: Mycophenolate
ingredients.note: Causes birth defects. Contact your doctor straight away; don't stop without advice.

ingredients.name: Thalidomide / lenalidomide
ingredients.note: Causes severe birth defects.

ingredients.name: Finasteride / dutasteride
ingredients.note: Can affect a male baby's development. Pregnant women shouldn't take or handle broken tablets.

ingredients.name: Testosterone / danazol
ingredients.note: Can affect the baby's development.

ingredients.name: Azathioprine
ingredients.note: Often continued under specialist care. Don't stop on your own.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.note: Food amounts and small doses for nausea are commonly used.

ingredients.name: Ashwagandha
ingredients.note: Traditionally avoided in pregnancy; not enough safety information.

ingredients.name: Fenugreek supplement
ingredients.note: Fine as food; concentrated supplements may stimulate the womb. Ask your doctor before taking them.

ingredients.name: St John's wort
ingredients.note: Not enough safety information, and it interacts with many medicines.

ingredients.name: Black or blue cohosh
ingredients.note: May cause contractions and other harm. Avoid unless supervised.

ingredients.name: Dong quai / pennyroyal
ingredients.note: Can stimulate the womb. Avoid.

ingredients.name: Castor oil (by mouth)
ingredients.note: Can trigger contractions. Don't use it to start labour unless your midwife or doctor advises.

ingredients.name: Aloe vera (by mouth)
ingredients.note: Aloe taken by mouth can cause contractions. Gel on the skin is fine.

ingredients.name: Turmeric / curcumin supplement
ingredients.note: Fine in food; concentrated supplements haven't been studied in pregnancy.

ingredients.name: Caffeine
ingredients.note: Keep total caffeine under 200 mg a day (about two cups of instant coffee), including from tea, cola and some cold medicines.
